title: Global mean-width minimization under linear symplectic maps
description:
This note settles Ahn and Kerman’s corrected Conjecture 1.6 on global minimum mean width of toric convex bodies under linear symplectic maps. It proves a stronger symmetry criterion: every compact convex body with nonempty interior that is invariant under the simultaneous quarter-turn J has minimum mean width over its linear symplectic orbit. The minimizing maps are exactly the orthogonal symplectic maps. The Lagrangian bidisk satisfies the same invariance and is a global linear corollary.

In the symplectic polar decomposition, the positive factor S is conjugate to its inverse by J. The two reciprocal images of a standard Gaussian have equal expected support. Convexity allows their midpoint C. Its Gaussian law equals that of the original vector plus independent noise with covariance C² − I. Conditional Jensen increases expected support. If S differs from identity, the positive-radius centered ball makes this Jensen gap strictly positive near zero, and hence in expectation.

The second arXiv revision claimed global toric and bidisk statements. Remark 1.7 of the corrected v3 withdrew the earlier toric proof. Its Theorem 1.4 and Proposition 1.12 establish local linear results. Green’s planar characterization already gives the planar inequality. The full special-linear minimum characterization by Giannopoulos and Milman uses isotropy of the spherical support-function weight. Quarter-turn symmetry alone does not ensure that isotropy. The note exhibits an unequal-radius product of disks whose mean width decreases under a determinant-one map. The theorem treats linear symplectic maps. The nonlinear bidisk first-variation question and the nonlinear global conjecture in the authors’ follow-up are separate. The primary literature search was bounded.

The six files give the authorless paper, LaTeX, bibliography, citation, repository checksum ledger and complete public evidence archive. The exact rational replay confirms 108 polar and covariance fixtures, 17,496 support and reciprocal-image checks, and the worked examples. The rotating view and the offline explorer display an area-preserving square squeeze that changes mean width from 8/π to 10/π at factor 2. Internally reviewed, not peer reviewed. No proof-assistant formalization is included.

ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the recovered proof under human direction. OpenAI Codex independently reviewed the mathematics. GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) checked primary sources and prepared the manuscript, exact replay and illustration. DannyExperiments is the project citation identity.
